subject: Post-call: deployment criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@cardinal-retail.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinal-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment criteria & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for your time earlier — good call. Quick recap + recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of Cardinal Retail's requirements from our discussion:
- Peak QPS (checkout search): ~450 RPS sustained during campaigns, 900 RPS spikes (30s windows)
- P95 generation latency target: <= 120 ms (user-facing autocompletion)
- Average request size: 80 tokens input, 30 tokens generated
- Data residency: US-only, but not strictly air-gapped
- Priority: consistent latency over absolute lowest cost for cart/checkout flows

Initial recommendation:
- Hosted API for prototyping, integration speed, and non-critical workloads (recommend TTL caching + prefix caching).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for checkout/autocomplete traffic due to high sustained throughput and tight P95s; dedicated capacity gives predictable tail latency and isolation.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Rishi (engineering) to validate our assumption about packing for 900 RPS spikes and provide a rough capacity sketch (GPU type + expected nodes).
2) We'll produce a short cost/latency model (attached) that compares Hosted vs Dedicated for your traffic profile.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up this week to review the model and decide on a pilot cadence.

Action items for Alex/Priya:
- Confirm whether the 900 RPS spike is soft (can be smoothed) or hard (must be handled without rejection).
- Share a small sample of typical request/response sizes (or anonymized logs) if possible.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-cost-model.xlsx (initial sketch), latency-throughput-snapshot.pdf (notes from call)

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@cardinal-retail.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinal-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment criteria & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- 900 RPS is a hard spike during major marketing pushes; we currently front it with autoscaling but see latency jitter.
- For the cutoff: if P95 exceeds 150 ms we start to see measurable drop in conversions.
- We can provide a 48-hour anonymized traffic dump (request/response sizes + timestamps).

Also, one question: is there a hybrid option where we run customer-facing checkout on Dedicated and keep lower-priority personalization on Hosted to save cost? Would Redwood's routing support that cleanly?

If so, we'd like to see a cost delta for a hybrid split (60% checkout on Dedicated, 40% personalization on Hosted).

Happy to meet Thursday afternoon if that works for Rishi and team.

— Alex
Alex Kim
Director, Platform Engineering
Cardinal Retail

Looping in Rishi to validate capacity assumptions and to outline the hybrid approach. Rishi — quick primer below (from the call):

- 450 RPS baseline, 900 RPS 30s spikes; P95 target <= 120 ms, conversion drop >>150 ms
- Request/response token distribution: ~80 in / ~30 out
- US-only region, no strict on-prem requirement for initial pilot

Could you review the attached model and confirm:
1) Best-fit Dedicated GPU type (NVIDIA A100x or equivalent) and estimated node count for the 900 RPS spikes while keeping P95 <= 120 ms.
2) Feasibility and typical SLOs for a hybrid routing setup (checkout on Dedicated, personalization on Hosted).
3) Rough lead times for Dedicated onboarding (reservation/commit durations) and recommended pilot length to gather tail latency metrics.

I've attached the cost model and a short snapshot from our call. Alex/Priya — feel free to add anything I missed.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: redwood-deploy-cost-model.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@cardinal-retail.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinal-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment criteria & next steps

Thanks — reviewed the model and notes. High level answers below and quick sizing sketch.

1) GPU recommendation & sizing:
- For 900 RPS spikes with ~110 tokens total (in+out) and tight P95 target, a Dedicated pool built on A100s (80GB) with 6 nodes (inference-optimized instances) looks like the right starting point. That gives headroom for KV cache and short bursts with continued batching.
- If you want lower-cost options and can accept slightly higher p95 (~160–180 ms), we can look at quantized V100-class fleets or mixed instance types and add autoscaling policies for spike windows.

2) Hybrid routing feasibility:
- Fully supported. Redwood routing policies can send production-critical inference (checkout) to Dedicated and route personalization/lightweight calls to Hosted. You get distinct SLOs, billing separation, and can A/B traffic easily.

3) Lead times & pilot cadence:
- Dedicated onboarding (reservation + infra provisioning): typical 2–3 weeks after contract sign; we can do a fast pilot on shared reserved capacity in 3–5 business days if urgency is high.
- Pilot recommendation: 2–4 weeks of live traffic with tail-metric collection (p50/p95/p99) and sampling of KV cache hit rates.

Next operational asks (from Rishi):
- Alex: share the anonymized 48-hr traffic dump and mark a 2-hour window with one of your upcoming spikes so we can target the pilot.
- Marissa: I'll update the cost sheet with a Hybrid column (60/40) and add two sizing scenarios (performance-first vs cost-balanced). Expect that by EOD tomorrow.

If this looks good Alex/Priya, let's lock a 30-min slot Thursday 3pm PT to review the updated model.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
